answer.text:
In the ordering logic design workshop on 12 November 2024, Lena Fischer described Acme's current practice as "Ninety-nine on everything, in theory, which is why we carry so much stock" (T07U0073, T07U0075). Tomas Lindholm then proposed "ninety-eight and ninety-five" as a reduction, saying "you should expect the inventory number to fall" (T07U0077-T07U0079), and Lena Fischer responded "Fine. Agreed." (T07U0083). The recorded agreement is therefore to reduce from the theoretical 99% to 98% and 95%, agreed in that workshop. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6]

Missing detail: the transcript does not record which categories or article groups receive 98% versus 95%. Tomas Lindholm's proposal states only "ninety-eight and ninety-five is a reduction" with no mapping (T07U0077-T07U0078), and no workshop output document is among the supplied evidence. The same session also recorded review cycles — "Daily order, sort of daily delivery on the fast lines, twice weekly below" (T07U0086) — but this delivery-cycle wording does not specify any service-level split by category. The category-to-service-level mapping is therefore unrecorded in the supplied evidence. [3] [4] [7]

Recommendation: treat the exact category-to-service-level mapping as unrecorded and confirm it from the workshop output document or with the meeting participants rather than assuming a split carried over; the supplied transcript supports only the 98/95 reduction itself (T07U0077-T07U0079, T07U0083). [3] [4] [5] [6]
